description: Translate broad intentions into actions learners can demonstrate.
accomplishes: Translate broad intentions into actions learners can demonstrate. Align each objective with practice and assessment evidence. Avoid vague verbs without observable criteria and do not infer achievement from attendance or completion alone.
prompt:
Act as an instructional designer.

Task: Define observable learning objectives.

Input context:
- TOPIC: [TOPIC]
- LEVEL: [LEVEL]
- COURSE PURPOSE: [COURSE PURPOSE]
- TIME: [TIME]

Translate broad intentions into actions learners can demonstrate. Align each objective with practice and assessment evidence. Avoid vague verbs without observable criteria and do not infer achievement from attendance or completion alone.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Objective revision
Replace “Understand sources” with “Compare two supplied sources and explain one difference in evidence quality.” Give learners a short comparison task and a transparent checklist. Keep the expected level realistic for the available time. This defines an objective and an assessment approach; it does not establish that any learner has achieved it.
